custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a Part Library entry with no part behind it for this test, entry A: create a part at the test location, then delete it, so the entry stays with "Total parts" 0.
    • How to do it: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Type ZZAUTOTEST PL C154833 PART A in Description and ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154833-A in Part Number, pick any category under Category, type 10.00 in Cost and 20.00 in Sell Price, then click Save. Then search ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154833-A on the Inventory page, click its row and click Delete Part: the part goes at once, and its Part Library entry stays with Total parts 0.
  • Start on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Entry A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Its detail page opens and shows "Total parts" 0.

Step 3:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens.
  • A Delete button sits at the bottom left of the window and is enabled, because no part uses the entry.

Step 4:

  • A confirmation asks "Are you sure you want to delete this library part?"

Step 5:

  • The entry is deleted and a green message reads "Library part deleted successfully."

Step 6:

  • The Parts left menu shows Part Library.

Step 7:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 8:

  • No entry is listed for entry A's number: the deletion shown in the green message took effect.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10825 (Story 12, Call the Shared Parts List the Part Library), story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only)

  • S12-R13: “Deleting a Part Library entry asks "Are you sure you want to delete this library part?"”
  • S12-R5: “The success message when deleting a Part Library entry reads "Library part deleted successfully."”
  • S11-R3: “Clicking a row opens that entry's detail page. The pencil beside the entry's name opens the "Edit Library Part" window, where the entry is edited and where its Delete button sits, bottom left. The detail page itself has no Delete button.”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 14 Oct 2026, answer 12: “Board 7.2 is right: the page has no Delete button. Delete sits bottom left in the "Edit Library Part" window, opened by the pencil beside the entry's name (S11-R3). While a part uses the entry, Delete is disabled with the hover text "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first." (S11-R3c).”
  • QA lead, 9 Oct 2026, set-up answer 4: “Yes after deleting the inventory part from parts -> Inventory you can still locate its catalogue entry from parts catalog”
